item.title: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious: Re: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Please note that I am not the most experienced user and am not qualified to give Greenlights. Please reach out to veteran authors and critters for some more informed crit.

here's the crit
wow look at that

I find the basic tenets of this idea very intriguing. The idea of a bonsai tree infecting the noosphere (collective human thought) is suitably mysterious and has great imagery potential. However, I believe that you'll find more success, both in the idea forums and the mainlist, if you can simplify your idea as much as possible. When I was having similar issues, this guide helped a lot: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/yourjouney-part-1

Another issue I have is that the exact nature of this anomaly seems to be a bit shaky. Here are some questions that I have that might inspire the development process:
Bonsai trees typically represent peace or tranquillity. What causes this one to be a symbol of the exact opposite?
There are multiple issues with the entire world instantly becoming aware of this phenomenon. What if everyone has this image in their minds, but cannot place it and typically don't pay it much mind?
Bonsai trees are tightly controlled by their gardeners to take on certain shapes and inspire certain feelings. What does the nature of this tree say about the person who grew it?

Overall, I believe this has promise. If you receive the necessary greenlights, please reach out to me with a draft. Have a good day!

item.title: Looking for critique on my SCP idea worked on it for a month now.: Re: Looking for critique on my SCP idea worked on it for a month now.
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Please note that I only have one article, and as such am not qualified to dispense greenlights. Please reach out to more experience reviewers for more informed critique.

As outlined in this guide: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/yourjouney-part-1 , SCP ideas that tend to succeed are simple, suitably interesting, and avoid feeling contrived. If I had to describe the concept you've laid out here, I would use the phrases "complex, (somewhat) interesting, and highly contrived."

The idea of a multiverse tree is neither here nor there on its own, as I could see the article being fantastic or incredibly boring depending on the execution. The main struggle you seem to be having is that you've added a plethora of unnecessary detail in order to convince either the reader or yourself that the idea is interesting. This results in a highly contrived appearance. It's also a common mistake, and I've made it myself multiple times. Excess of detail or lore doesn't have any intrinsic appeal.

Whether you decide to try and refine this idea (difficult) or start from scratch (my recommendation), my advice is this: start not with an anomaly, but with a story or a feeling that you're passionate about. Design the anomaly around this idea, and then simplify it as much as you possibly can.

Have a good day!

item.title: A Treasure Chest for (media) Pirates: A Treasure Chest for (media) Pirates
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Normal, but with "Notable Files" log.

Elevator Pitch: An anomaly where filesharing sites and FTP servers spontaneously obtain all pieces of media, even lost media with no evidence for its existence.

Central Narrative: Upon the first manifestation of the anomaly on ftp://[REDACTED], The Foundation, upon discovering mountains of classified material, and world governments, upon discovering mountains of illegal content, collaborate to shut down sites affected by SCP-XXXX. One server is archived by the Foundation, and contains the presumably infinite (yet 100TB in size) archive.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Notable content is recorded on a log by Information Researcher Jones. Throughout the logs, he documents his experiences and how his mental state is affected from seeing some of the more disturbing content in the archive.

Additional Notes: The concept of this is essentially "What if the Foundation was responsible for shutting down so many filesharing sites?".

item.title: Of sirens and memetic agents: Re: Of sirens and memetic agents
item.content:encoded:
1) It's not THAT family-friendly when her mere image causes violence in men. Also, don't introduce it as a "modern take" or "gender-bending"; it's just marketing copy that turns off a lot of people.

If that's all your story has going for it, then it needs something else.

2) I'm honestly interested in how they held the interviews; that alone would be interesting to see. I'm thinking it would be via text-only, making it sort of interesting.

3) That said. you need to seriously build this up somehow. As it stands right now it's probably better in the Tales section than as a straight article. This relies solely on its narrative elements to be interesting, rather than on the anomaly itself. Thus, while this is an interesting story, especially if the humor is played up, I'm not sure how "lesbian siren" would play as an article.

item.title: Tale about the fall of the SCP Foundation.: Tale about the fall of the SCP Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: The fall of the SCP Foundation is happening. Almost all of the SCPs have breached containment and are roaming the world. Site-[REDACTED] has almost been completely destroyed. The foundation is trying its best to re-contain all of the escaped SCPs

Central Narrative: One of the survivors of the site wide containment breach was a containment specialist, Victor. He was inside of the cafeteria eating his lunch when an unknown group broke into the site and freed almost all of the hostile SCPs. Victor escaped the site.

Now he has to survive in the most intense apocalypse known to mankind.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Its unique because Victor is dealing with many SCPs that have breached containment, and are possibly hostile. He has to survive a long and stressful time.

Additional Notes: I need help with the central narrative and the hook/attention grabber.

item.title: Dissociative Somnia Phenomenon: Dissociative Somnia Phenomenon
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: YES

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch:
An event in which an individual, usually that suffers from night terrors, will experience a dissociative episode(out of body experience) by "dreaming" about dying or killing. The dreams represent with precision the death of a person close to them, who will die within the next few weeks. Attempts to prevent this fate will often result in catastrophic outcomes.

Central Narrative:
The Inevitability of death and acceptance of loss.

Hook:
It's the classic "how would you react if you knew someone that you like is going to die?". I believe this concept to be interesting enough for the small intended size of the article.

Additional notes:
I'm not a hundred percent sure there isn't anything like this on the site already. I've looked around and found nothing that's close, but if there is, please, feel free to warn me.

item.title: Complete Desolation: Re: Complete Desolation
item.content:encoded:
The obvious problem you have is that it's based on a tac-nuke; while it's always fun to go into what a tac-nuke can do, they are just unlikely to target something small enough to be taken out with one. Upgrading it just creates bigger problems. You'd do better with an epidemic or invasion, which have been known to take out towns.

It would also be harder to keep the city out of the news.

It is worth noting that experimentation would be able to determine if he is truly schizophrenic or is actually talking to ghosts; The Foundation would be able to determine that. If he truly is talking to ghosts, then The Foundation would have specialists that would love to talk to him. If he's merely schizophrenic, The Foundation getting him help would make for some interesting debates similar to whether or not he could leave the town.

Otherwise, an excellent start. It should be interesting to see where this goes.

Hmmm… I haven't given that one much consideration. (As I think you can tell.) I think that the thing that inspired me to make it a millipede was a picture I saw of a giant extinct millipede species. Maybe it could be one of those that managed to survive somehow.

Ok, this is my favorite part. It's a germaphobe because in this universe a plague was what wiped out the rest of it's species. (Man they could have really used 049.) It was the only one who could fend off the plague using it's anomalous properties.

This is actually the most interesting aspect at the moment

I know.

maybe give it cleaning supplies and have it join the site cleaning crew.

Haha! Actually that might be a good idea… especially if that's it's only anomalous property. Come to think of it I actually really like that idea.

I'm going to change the SCP Idea to be a millipede that is able to kill all germs that are near it. (Exact distance yet to be determined.) Scrap everything else this is what the idea is now. Thank you for the ideas! I have edited the original post to represent this.

item.title: Two Dimensional Love: Re: Two Dimensional Love
item.content:encoded:
If you expanded on the "lovesick" side of the trope a bit, it could be interesting, where the doll punishes the man for leaving her alone for too long. Also, the western otaku angle would be interesting, as well as fit into the AWCY philosophy.

It would also be interesting to look into her sentience, especially in terms of various Japanese revenge tales. That is, is she based on a real woman who was wronged in real life, and the doll gives her a chance to get that revenge.

It's a good idea, it just needs to be fleshed out some.

item.title: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.: Re: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.
item.content:encoded:
It's an interesting idea, but limited in terms of testing (once The Foundation has a few solid tests in terms of the progression they'll likely stop). The two biggest problems are how to stop or even reset the progression, and how to actually find it.

Also, you may want to consider that just creating an SCP that's annoying is usually not enough, but has to have some sort of narrative background to it, such as where it comes from, was it designed by a group with a specific agenda in mind, or even an accident of evolution.

It's a good basic idea, but needs to be fleshed out some.

item.title: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror with a tinge of dark comedy.

Page Layout (Optional): A standard SCP article included with experiences of D-Class dealing with the SCP and footnotes of some unusual instances of the SCP

Elevator Pitch: The first instance of SCP-??? is a small gnat that appears in the affected individual’s room anywhere from 10 P.M to 2 A.M and is first seen flying around a light source in the room or heard buzzing past the individual’s ear. This gnat proves extremely annoying, being nearly impossible to catch and contain for the night and will buzz by the individual’s ear just as they’re falling asleep. However, the gnat is very easy to kill, seemingly stopping if it’s approached with the intent of swatting it. But, killing the gnat will activate the next “stage” of SCP-???, this time a fly. Killing this instance again “ramps” up the SCP to a mosquito the next night, and so on and so on until you get mosquitoes with malaria, murder hornets, and other terrible crawlies. However, no matter what stage you’re on, they all follow the same rule of the insect being able to fly around and of being easy to kill but nearly impossible to catch and contain.

Central Narrative: I want to focus on how D-Class subjects either cope or go insane from this terrible predicament, and how bad it can get if you keep ramping up the stages.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A crawly in your rooms at night is something we’ve all dealt with at some point, so I feel like that familiar premise combined with my unique (hopefully) idea activates that deep fear of insects in the reader.

Additional Notes: I’m not positive if I want to have it ramp up to the point of being unbearable, or plateau at a certain point so it’s not enough to be completely devastating, but the annoyance is enough to slowly eat away at the individual. Curious on what your thoughts are.

item.title: Two Dimensional Love: Re: Two Dimensional Love
item.content:encoded: Apologies for the needless edge, I based the idea on a nightmare I had and rushed into it. The idea was that the doll was based on the "yandere" anime trope, and I planned to expand on that in the experiment logs with incidents such as a victim being brought out of the trance only to be butchered the next time he goes in, with the implication being that the doll doesn't like being "abandoned". But I really like the cultural appropriation idea, what if instead of a lonely Japanese man it's a Western otaku who ends up being killed by it due to messing with things he doesn't truly understand?

item.title: The innate nature of things.: Re: The innate nature of things.
item.content:encoded:
Hi Thanks for the feedback. You asked some questions directly so I'm going to answer them here.

+ show block
– hide block

Is this a 'mechanism' as in like, a physical machine? or a mechanism as in an abstract process?

It's an abstract process. Because the whole environment of the universe is a product of this machine on both a physical and metaphysical level the machine can leave abstract triggers that allow you to interface with it. If you know anything about computers it's a little like an OS providing code running under it with access to system calls that can be used to request more memory and print stuff to the screen. Its like a system call embedded in reality on an abstract level.

You would use these triggers with your mind but it would be very difficult. Something only a few people can do. I'll leave the actual experience of using one of these triggers mostly up to the imagination but indicate that it's something fundamentally difficult to express in words (hence why it's such a hard skill to teach).

What's the security like here? How does it make progress harder?

This feels…like a really weird way to solve this problem

I agree. This was little bit of a throwaway line.

In my head I imagined big doors with complicated mechanical locks that take weeks to crack. Shifting hallways and an impossible to map structure. This is a tad generic though so I will probably try and develop this before my next idea draft.

Regarding the narrative being passive I'd say I agree with that. I'm going to go away and think about all of this before coming back and rewriting this document. I'm very confident that I can polish this up.

Your feedback has been indispensable and I hope you will take another look when the next version is ready.

Thanks for your time.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight On My Idea: Re: Seeking Greenlight On My Idea
item.content:encoded:
My apologies on being too vague. Allow me to try and respond to some of your concerns. (Still not very good at formatting, but I'll try)

What do these interviews/interrogations actually like…add narratively here? My concern is that they're going to be either relatively info-dumpy or relatively contentless depending on how co-operative the people being interviewed are.

I have a multitude of ideas for these interviews which (as I haven't begun writing them yet) aren't super fleshed out, but have, what I think is, a good basis.

  • A local who's fountain, one day, produced very hot water, but only once- this one is more comedic, to open the logs on a lighter note. Interviewers will try and focus the question on the fountains appearance and disappearance itself, but the interviewed man will be hyperfocused on the hot water. As these people believe, and perceive, these fountains as completely natural phenomenon, it'd be like waking up one day to your grass being a neon red, and being unable to prove it to anyone.
  • One or two individuals who have lived in the area for JUST UNDER the time it takes for the memetic effects to take hold. They will be noticably distressed and nervous, aware that something is taking place out of the ordinary, but unable to question it fully. These are more worldbuilding
  • Interview with a police chief/undecided government official of some sort. The Foundation tries to see if any of the upper-caste of society, leader of any small religious group, etc, has any connection to these fountains, but comes up empty handed, and starts to become weary on further investigation
  • A junior researcher comes across something peculiar. In one of the more isolated, backwoods properties of the township, an older man is seen praying to his fountain every Tuesday. This totally breaks the previous conception that everyone affected sees the fountains as normal. The man is interviewed and interrogated, and is identified as one of the few remaining members of the nearby Ramapough Lenape natives. He is stubborn to give information at first, but a search of his property reveals a journal which has been logging the appearances of the fountains for the past few decades.

Then, I plan to detail the log the man has written, which will give further insight into the phenomenon of this SCP. I understand the "Native American curse" concept may be somewhat overdone, not entirely sure, but I think I can take this in an interesting direction while also bringing to light some of the slights against the Ramapough Lenape.

The log will stretch back to the mid-70s/early-80s, with a preface, where the man recounts losing close family members to contaminated water and food due to a (very real) toxic waste landfill used by Ford in which affordable housing was constructed upon. Everything after that in the log, will be mostly excluded/expunged, menial information (pH testing, and marking the times the fountains appear) as to avoid massive exposition. The township he's selected to test his revenge on is a perfectly isolated, echo chamber of a community. A place where the population would hardly question, or have the dialogue to discuss, such a phenomenon, before it takes hold. An incubation chamber for a more diabolical scheme. The extent, and area of attack of this scheme, will be left to the reader, somewhat.

After holding the man for a period of one week, and maintaining testing of his fountain, Foundation researchers will notice a new presence of dangerous levels of lead contaminants. Upon release, the fountains will return to their normal state of producing clean water, but the damage is done- many residents have been killed or are seriously ill after consumption of the water. They are all, however, unable to recognize that the fountains were the cause of this.

An addendum will tie things up, from one of the interviewers, warning that further disruption of the phenomenon could be genocidal, and to focus all efforts on surveillance of the identified suspect, to avoid spread of the phenomenon out of the affected township.

you gotta give everything away here btw like if a reviewer doesn't have a full idea of what your idea actually is, it's very hard for them to judge whether it's a good idea.

I hope this cleared things up, a little. If anything is too overboard, doesn't seem to work (in your eyes), let me know. I am more than happy to rework this as much as needed, even from the ground up. I really feel like I have something here that can be informative, unsettling, and neuron-firing, without being a super scary bloody beast, or a gore fest or super powerful humanoid. If I am wrong in that feeling, please just let me know.

item.title: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights): Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Some questions and info that might help you see the issues here, and point you down a more productive path:

Why is it a millipede? Not just in the mechanical sense, but why, for the purposes of the story, is it a millipede rather than a centipede, or a robot, or a bowl of nachos with legs? There should be a why, at least in your mental notes. If there isn't: Why is it a millipede?

Why does it attack things? Again, if there isn't a reason: Why does it attack things?

Why is it a germaphobe? (This is actually the most interesting aspect at the moment, btw. Zero sarcasm: maybe give it cleaning supplies and have it join the site cleaning crew.)

What makes this an SCP? The Foundation has loads of giant bugs in containment. What makes this one require Special containment procedures instead of "lock it up and feed it periodically"

Potentially relevant info regarding millipedes: In the early days of land-dwelling life, millipedes were some of the largest creatures on Earth, some species measuring around 2 meters. They had no known predators. Almost all species of millipede (past and present) are herbivores. Their survival mechanisms are almost entirely defensive measures- they curl up, some taste bad or excrete mildly irritating chemicals, some have bristles…it's all protection, no offense. Some of the most harmless creatures on earth, really.
